title: Arkret MLS Governance Proof Bundle
description: Complete-materialization proof bundle used by a light client to verify an MLS full-profile governance binding against an accepted Seal. v1 deliberately carries the complete covered-event digest manifest and every non-bottom control-state leaf: a selective proof over server-chosen leaves cannot prove that a policy, capability, membership, or metadata leaf was not omitted. proof_request_digest binds the normalized acquisition identity, including the verifier's trusted anchor; bundle_digest is the content address of the complete canonical bundle. accepted_seal_id alone is not a Bundle cache key. A future compact profile requires a separately registered completeness-proof construction.

proof_request_digest.description: sha256(UTF-8('arkret-mls-governance-proof-request-v1\n') || RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes of the exact proof_request object). The verifier MUST recompute it from its request before using or caching the response.

bundle_digest.description: Content address: sha256(UTF-8('arkret-mls-governance-proof-bundle-v1\n') || RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes of this complete Bundle with bundle_digest omitted). A verifier MUST recompute it after schema and request binding checks.

materialization_profile.description: The only v1 profile. covered_event_digests is the entire recursive covered_set of accepted_seal_id and control_state is the entire sorted set of non-bottom joined control cells committed by its state_root.

trusted_anchor_seal_id.description: MUST equal proof_request.trusted_anchor_seal_id bit-for-bit. This is a Seal id the verifier already trusts through authenticated Realm bootstrap or prior successful verification. Presence in this bundle never makes an anchor trusted.

accepted_seal_id.description: Id of the accepted Seal whose control_event_set_root and state_root authenticate this bundle. It MUST identify the final Seal in seal_path.

seal_path.description: Topologically ordered Seal extension path beginning at the trusted anchor (or its direct successor) and ending at accepted_seal_id. The verifier validates every id, predecessor edge, notary authorization and signature; bundle order is not itself trusted.

covered_event_digests.description: Complete recursive covered_set of accepted_seal_id in canonical wire-value order. The verifier MUST reject duplicates or non-canonical order and MUST recompute accepted Seal.control_event_set_root with the Seal RFC 6962 domain-separated Merkle rules.

control_state.description: Complete canonical cell-id ordered materialization of every non-bottom joined control cell under accepted_seal_id. Bottom cells MUST be omitted and separately cause any dependent full-profile binding to fail closed. The verifier recomputes accepted Seal.state_root over this exact array.

frontier_events.description: Complete set of signed Control Move envelopes named by governance_binding.membership_frontier. The verifier recomputes each Event digest, requires it in covered_event_digests, checks its effects target the registered membership/device/lifecycle coverage families for effective_scope, and rejects missing, extra, duplicate, cross-Realm or cross-scope events.

trusted_anchor_seal_id.description: Seal id already trusted by this verifier. The service MUST construct seal_path from this exact anchor (or its direct successor) and MUST NOT silently substitute a newer, older, or service-selected anchor. A bootstrap client uses the Realm genesis/compaction Seal only after validating it through its authenticated Realm bootstrap, join, snapshot, or equivalent trust package.

proof_request.description: Authenticated account-client query input. The service derives all governance roots and membership_frontier from one accepted Seal view; callers MUST NOT supply any root or frontier. The caller MUST name one locally trusted anchor. If the service cannot prove a path from that exact anchor to the target accepted Seal, it returns mls_governance_anchor_unreachable and MUST NOT suggest or substitute an untrusted anchor. Genesis requests MUST use previous_epoch=0 and next_epoch=0; commit requests MUST use next_epoch=previous_epoch+1.
